I gotta say these last few months have been pretty brutal. I was diagnosed back in 2011 when I had my first and only resection, and I've been doing great since then... until about the start of the new year. I'm going in for a scope on the 15th to check some things out, but until then, how are you? What's your story?
How are you all feeling? What's your story?

I was diagnosed earlier this year. I started getting pains in my stomach last summer, but put it down to stress at work and tried to stick it out. They just kept getting worse until the constant pain and exhaustion were interfering with my work so much that I had to leave my job. I lost about three stone in the space of a few months because I felt so sick all the time I couldn't eat. They didn't really get any better after I left work, but my doctor kept telling me that it was still just stress. In March I started getting a pain in my hip that felt like a pulled muscle, but it quickly got so bad that I couldn't walk and I started getting fevers, shakes and dizzy spells. I finally saw a different doctor who referred me to the hospital to have a scan and it turned out that I had a huge abscess deep in my body cavity. I was in hospital for two weeks while that was being treated and it was then that I was diagnosed with Crohn's. A month after I got out, it came back and I ended up in hospital for another week and a half, so I spent a total of about two months on antibiotics.

My doctors don't think surgery is a good option for me at the moment as I already had a resection when I was younger (completely unrelated to Crohn's) and they were worried about cutting too much out too soon. I'm meant to be starting Remicade on Wednesday, but the inflammation has been quite bad recently so I think I'm going to ask for a blood test first to make sure the infection isn't coming back again.

I'm glad you found a doctor eventually that was able to diagnosis it, but holy hell man, I am sorry that it took that long.

Best of luck on starting Remicade. After years of trying other meds, it was what finally worked for me. As long as I avoid trigger foods (corn and nuts for me), then I am 100% all the time on it. I really hope it works out for you.

I was diagnosed about 10 years ago now. I was in senior year of high school and started constantly having stomach pains. But they were never debilitating or truly constant. What made me finally see is a doc was the large amounts of blood that started coming out with my movements. Well, it wasn't even so much WITH my movements, and these would be all on their own. I remember the first time I saw the toilet paper bright red and looked down to see a bowl full of blood was one of the scariest moments. No more, 'oh I am fine it'll pass'. Something was seriously wrong.

Well after finding out it was Crohns, I was on any combo of anti inflammatories and steriods for about 2 years. Nothing worked. It was miserable. I was missing out on being a kid right out of high school. I couldn't do much at all. Finally I was put on Remicade, and it was like night and day. I felt like a new person. I saw on it for 2 or 3 years, flare free.

Then I started traveling a lot for work. I would mis infusions, forget about them, etc. Finally they took me off of it, and told me I may be in remission for a while. Well, I was for the most part. For around 4 years I had maybe a small flare a year. Nothing bad, I could just feel it a little.

Cut to spring 2014. Started getting bad pains, keeping me from running, biking, hiking, all the things I do on a regular basis. Once I finally got it scoped, it turns out I had a large abscess in my gut due to a fistula that looped my small intestine back into itself. I was giving the choice of trying to fight it for six months with medicine or get a resection. The doc said the medicine was like a 50/50 shot, but if I was worried about surgery I could try it first. I had my first kid on the way (twins!) within 4 months, and couldn't imagine dealing with the pain and fatigue of this if the medicine didn't work. So, last summer I had a resection.

Initially they said it would be about 18 inches removed, enough that I would always have liquidy BM's and might have to take vitamin supplements the rest of my life. Luckily once I woke up they said they were able to get it back together after 'only' taking 11 inches. I felt like a new man once I was out. But, now I am back on Remicade to make sure I don't have more flares.

Thankfully mom understood and allowed her to stay so we brought her stuff inside and by that point both of us just wanted to sleep. For the previous few months she was very upset, depressed and just not herself at all because of her home issues. But when we laid down in bed together, it felt like the weight of the world lifted off our shoulders. Both of us originally planned on going right to bed so the TV and lights were out.
